title: Conditional κ = 0.001651390457077212: PR648 complex supplier with the merged #589 bit supplier (outdated, independent)
body:
> **Outdated, independent composition.** This was done concurrently with jeremykothe2's #649 (κ 0.001652528731617094: #589 bit supplier plus a dissolved owner map on gauge44) and #652 (κ 0.001652760598550299). Both are higher than this PR. It is submitted as an independent replay of the #589 bit swap applied to #648 alone: the owner map is unchanged. It makes no record claim over #649 or #652.

## Summary

κ = **412847614269303/250000000000000000 = 0.001651390457077212**, +0.01781% over #648 (0.001651096360425895). The complex side binds.

## Why the swap is valid

- #648 states its complex side certifies b = 0.0016541221, above #543's bit c = 0.0016538270, so **the bit side binds** and κ is the #543 cap. The outer assembly sets s = min(c, (1−β)·b), so a larger admissible c raises κ until the complex side binds.
- #589 (DreamingOfClouds, c = 0.001733427039589844234749) is merged. It is preserved on main at `research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/tune/EXPECTED.json` (the same git blob, e293ddc5, as at #589's head a5afc8c). Main's reviews cite #543 only because their compositions were complex-limited. The hyperplane599 review says "#589 is better bit headroom but is not needed by this complex-limited composition", and the family588 review calls #555 "useful headroom". No dispute or retraction appears in the #555 or #589 threads.
- **Retained bit premises** (as in #545 and #555): a v = 111 bit supplier in the outer assembly, and pooled-cell bit hosting. #543 uses the same pooled-cell contract, and neither satisfies #458's stricter one-helper-per-family rule.
- #555's own c (0.001733052823) gives the identical κ, since the complex side binds either way.

## What changed (one commit on #648, `research/gauge44-repack/` only)

- `inputs/PR589-EXPECTED.json`: main's #589 receipt, byte for byte.
- `code/assemble.py` reads that receipt in place of `inputs/PR543-EXPECTED.json`. It then:
  - checks the receipt's git blob id, its c, and the word parameters (v = 111, R = 439, decoder constant 63 = 9·7);
  - replaces the literal bit deficit 9,984 (#543's v = 120) with the nine-stage identity T(8v − 9·cst) = 32·321 = 10,272;
  - computes the binding side (`complex`) instead of hard-coding it;
  - records the supplier provenance.
- `verify_global.py` asserts the vendored receipt equals main's copy, and `data/UPSTREAM-PINS.json` pins main's copy by sha256.
- `data/SPEC.json`: only `expected.kappa`, `kappa_decimal` and `conservative_kappa_decimal` change. They were re-derived by the package's own discovery → `code/freeze_spec.py` → strict chain, and every other recorded value matched.
- `README.md` gains a header section, and `MANIFEST.json` is regenerated.

Unchanged: the owner map, PLAN, the construction, the invoice, both exact moment engines (the bit bad-residue surcharge is retained, and #589's profile is accepted at c and rejected at c + 10⁻²⁴ by both engines), the 47-inequality outer assembly, the outer controls (next_grid, zero_eta, zero_beta, unit_beta), and all 69 admission controls.

## Verification

Run on macOS with CPython 3.11, from a fresh `git archive` of this commit:

- `verify_manifest.py`: PASS (87 files).
- `construction/reproduce.py --until phases`: PASS phases. It rebuilt the local supplier from #635 (a6895a6); the construction files are unchanged from #648.
- `verify_global.py --main . --local <fresh local>`: PASS for restore-parent, bind, emit, audit, invoice, assembly and admission-controls (69 rejected). It printed `PASS_GAUGE44_NATIVE_EXACT_GLOBAL_ASSEMBLY 0.001651390457077212`. The conservative (pre-#559) complex charge passes at 0.00165139045419947.

```
git fetch https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds.git a6895a69f8ad98ab45777b03e9e6f48888c39f6f
mkdir -p /tmp/gauge44-pr635 && git archive FETCH_HEAD research/complex-571-cold14-st2 | tar -x -C /tmp/gauge44-pr635
python -B research/gauge44-repack/verify_manifest.py
python -B research/gauge44-repack/construction/reproduce.py --main . --pr635 /tmp/gauge44-pr635 --out /tmp/g44b-local --until phases
python -B research/gauge44-repack/verify_global.py --main . --local /tmp/g44b-local/local --work /tmp/g44b-global
```

## Scope

The same premises as #645 and #648 apply: the all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, normalized wrappers, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, exact recovery, analytic transfer and bit H1–H5. The #555/#545 bit premises above also apply. This is a conditional finite construction, with no unconditional theorem and no Lean certification.
